topic: The Secret of Learning: An Intuitive Guide to Backpropagation
target_audience: Introductory Data Science students or curious tech enthusiasts

sections.title: The Goal: The Error Gap
lecture_lines: Neural networks learn by adjusting thousands of tiny knobs.
These knobs are weights that control the network's output.
Our goal is to minimize the Error Gap, or Loss.
animations: Show a stylized machine with several [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/knob.svg] labeled Weights (#00BFFF).
Show a target bullseye and an arrow hitting 2m above it.
Draw a red bracket (#FF0000) between arrow and bullseye labeled Error Gap.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Forward Flow
lecture_lines: In the forward flow, data moves through layers.
Inputs are weighted, summed, and activated to produce guesses.
This guess is compared to reality to measure mistakes.
animations: Represent input data as a cat icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cat.png] moving into the network.
Show neurons lighting up sequentially from left to right (#FFFF00).
Display final output 70% Dog (#FF4500) next to label Cat.

sections.title: Intuition: The Blame Game
lecture_lines: Backpropagation is like a "blame game" for errors.
We look at the final mistake and trace backward.
We identify which knobs contributed most to the error.
Each weight gets a share of the "blame" signal.
Only those responsible are adjusted to fix the result.
animations: Highlight the 70% Dog [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/dog.svg] error with a red Blame label (#FF0000).
Animate a red pulse moving backward from Output to the Chef layer.
Highlight the Chef knob with a bright flash (#FFFF00) indicating high blame.
Distribute smaller pulses to Waiter and Supplier layers.
Animate the Chef knob rotating slightly to show adjustment.

sections.title: Visualizing the Gradient (The Slope)
lecture_lines: The Gradient shows the direction of the Error Hill.
Positive slopes mean increasing the weight increases the error.
Negative slopes mean increasing the weight decreases the error.
animations: Create a 2D curve representing the Loss Landscape [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/hill.svg] (#00FF00).
Place a ball [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ball.svg] on the hill [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/hill.svg] with a tangent line (#FFFFFF).
Animate the ball [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ball.svg] moving down the slope toward the local minimum.

sections.title: The Chain Rule: Connecting the Layers
lecture_lines: The Chain Rule connects local changes to final errors.
We multiply sensitivities layer by layer moving backwards.
This propagates the error signal through the entire network.
It reveals how hidden layers impact the final outcome.
Simple multiplication links all layers into one learning system.
animations: Show nodes A, B, and C connected by arrows in a row.
Label edges with 3x and 2x sensitivity values (#FFD700).
Animate a red signal pulsing backward from C to B then B to A.
Display the calculation 3 * 2 = 6 appearing above the nodes.
Highlight the entire backward path A<-B<-C with a glow (#FFD700).

sections.title: The Update: Gradient Descent
lecture_lines: Now, we take a small step against the gradient.
We subtract a fraction of the gradient from weights.
This fraction is controlled by the "Learning Rate."
Small steps prevent overcorrecting and ensure stable learning.
Repeating this process thousands of times achieves high accuracy.
animations: Show a weight value W = 10 next to a machine knob.
Animate a Learning Rate factor (e.g. 0.02) appearing.
Animate the knob turning, decreasing W to 9.8 (#7CFC00).
Show a small arrow pointing down the slope of a mini-hill.
Show the Error Gap bracket from Section 1 shrinking in size.
